content.thinking:
I need to write the root cause and executive summary without restating the given cost figures as if I'd calculated them myself, since those numbers came from the shop's own records, not my computation. I can still reference the timeframe of the incident (11:27–11:33) descriptively since that's factual context, not a derived figure.

I should flag my key assumptions clearly: that the flag was enabled deliberately though no record shows who or why, that recovery correlates with the flag revert, that the ZeroDivisionError likely hit accounts with zero-value denominators, that no deploy was found in the 24-hour lookback so an out-of-window change isn't ruled out, and that the background ~1% ClientDisconnected errors are unrelated noise. The executive summary should describe the impact as account page failures for shoppers, avoiding internal component names.

assumptions: The flag flip at 11:27 is treated as the trigger because the error signature changed exactly at that minute and cleared after the revert; the correlation was not independently verified against the flag provider's audit trail beyond the single recent change it reported.
Who enabled monthly-spend-feature, and why, is not recorded in anything reviewed here.
The lookback for production changes was 24 hours. A code change older than that which shipped the defective path was not ruled out, only judged unsupported.
The low level of pre-incident account-page errors (ClientDisconnected, shoppers closing connections) is assumed to be normal background and unrelated to this incident.
The exact condition that makes the divisor zero in spend_summary.py:35 was not confirmed from the code or from failing requests; it is inferred from the exception type and location.
Impact is assumed to be limited to the account page, since that is the only surface that appears in the logs reviewed; no downstream or partner effects were checked.
The service is assumed to have stayed healthy after 11:34; confirmation rests on a single check at that time, not on continued observation.
input.executive_summary: On 23 September 2026, a newly switched-on feature for the account page caused a share of shoppers to get an error instead of their account page. The failures began at 11:27 UTC and stopped at 11:33 UTC, when the account page returned to its normal behaviour. Only the account page was affected; shoppers who reloaded after recovery saw the page work normally, and nothing needed to be corrected in shopper data afterwards. Automated response picked up the alert at 11:32 UTC, traced the failures to the feature that had just been switched on, switched it back off, and confirmed the page had returned to normal before closing out the mitigation. A draft code change to fix the underlying defect was opened the same hour, and the feature remains off until that fix lands.
input.root_cause: The feature flag `monthly-spend-feature` was turned on for io-shop at 11:27 UTC (ramping from ~29% of evaluations to fully on within a minute), which made a previously unreachable code path live; that path raises ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:35 while rendering the account page, so every request that hit the new path failed. No deploy or release was recorded on the service in the 24 hours before onset, so the flag flip — not a code change — is what put the defect into the serving path.
